messages:
maria (AE): Quick ask — large payments customer wants a single-page summary we can hand to their auditors: BYOK options, whether Redwood ever sees plaintext, rotation SLA, and expected timeline to run a POC. They flagged nCipher HSM as primary requirement and asked if hosted plan is allowed.

ben (sales-eng): Short summary we usually give: (1) BYOK gateway (mutual-TLS) keeps keys in customer HSM (Redwood never sees key material or plaintext). (2) CloudHSM/KMS import: keys can be imported/wrapped into customer's cloud KMS and Redwood integrates normally. (3) For strict on-prem HSM we recommend Private or Dedicated to meet isolation regs, but hosted is possible if customer exposes a peered gateway.

leo (solutions): POC timeline: 2	6 weeks depending on cert exchange windows. Typical plan: 3-phase POC — (A) connectivity + cert exchange (2-3 days after kickoff), (B) functional ops (encrypt/decrypt, audit export) + perf run (3-5 days), (C) rotation drill + attestation (1-2 days). Need HSM admin + infra lead from customer.

irene (security): For auditors: we can provide a one-page attestation plus artifacts. Attestation includes: architecture diagram, signed audit log sample (key_id, operation, timestamp, request_id), BYOK appendix language, and our SOC2/ISO summary. Important: state clearly whether keys are imported. Language we use: "When BYOK gateway mode is selected, cryptographic key material remains in the Customer's HSM and is not exported to Redwood. Redwood stores only ciphertext and key references. All decrypt operations are executed in the Customers KMS/HSM."

maria (AE): They also want explicit rotation SLA: how quickly can we switch to a new key and guarantee no request failures?

leo (solutions): Operationally: with active/passive dual-key rewrap and cache invalidation we can achieve a rotation window typically <5 minutes for p50 path for requests that respect cache TTLs. Real number depends on client-side cache TTL and propagation. For our formal SLA we offer a documented rotation playbook and can run a rotation drill during the POC.

ben (sales-eng): Pricing: onboarding connector fee one-time $8k	6k for CloudHSM import or gateway setup; hosted connector recurring $750	1.5k/mo depending on support level; if they require Private/Dedicated add-ons, pricing shifts to reserved capacity model + platform license. Zeroization attestation (if keys were previously imported) is a one-time service line item (~$2k). I'll build a quick workbook if they share expected crypto ops/day and target p99 latency.

maria (AE): Can you paste the short auditor-facing summary I can email? Keep it to one page.

irene (security): Heres a compact draft you can send. Copy-paste only: \n
"Redwood BYOK and HSM summary for auditors:\n\n- BYOK modes:\n  1) Gateway (mutual-TLS): Customer HSM remains authoritative. Redwood sends encrypted payloads to the Customer gateway; decryption occurs within the Customer HSM. Redwood does not have access to unencrypted key material or plaintext.\n  2) Cloud KMS import (CloudHSM-backed): Customer may import wrapped key material into their cloud KMS backed by HSM. Redwood integrates with the customer's cloud KMS; Redwood holds ciphertext and key references only.\n\n- Rotation: Redwood supports dual-key active/passive rotation with cache invalidation. Typical rotation drill completes in under 5 minutes; exact window depends on client cache TTL and network propagation. Redwood will execute rotation playbook jointly with Customer during POC.\n\n- Zeroization: If key material remains in Customer HSM, Redwood cannot zeroize keys; we will coordinate and provide attestation once Customer performs zeroization. If key material was imported into Redwood environment under Customer authorization, Redwood will perform zeroization upon verified written request and provide signed attestation.\n\n- Audit artifacts available: signed usage logs (key_id, op, ts, request_id), architecture diagram, BYOK appendix, SOC2/ISO summary, and FIPS compatibility statement for HSMs we integrate with.\n\n- Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted is possible with a peered gateway and strict routing. For customers requiring physical isolation we recommend Dedicated/Private deployment.\n\nFor follow-up please provide: HSM vendor and model, expected crypto ops/sec, p50/p99 latency targets, and preferred POC kickoff dates."\n
leo (solutions): Nice. I'll attach a short checklist they can fill: HSM admin contact, cert PEM, sample key_id OR gateway endpoint, expected qps, test dataset.

ben (sales-eng): I'll own pricing workbook — maria, paste estimated ops and desired SLOs and I'll send back a line-item estimate.

infra-bot: Created ticket: POC-5127 BYOK/nCipher POC. Owner: leo (solutions). Attachments: BYOK one-pager (draft), rotation-playbook (stub).

maria (AE): Thanks team  I'll send the one-pager to the customer and ask for the checklist details. If they insist on contractual zeroization language, I'll loop in legal and irene for sign-off. :white_check_mark:
